description:
“Heart and Body” introduces a new community under Pierpaolo Piccioli’s creative direction, naming Winona Ryder, Roh Yoonseo and Harris Dickinson as brand ambassadors alongside Friends of the House Danielle Deadwyler, Havana Rose Liu, Labrinth, Hudson Williams, Mona Tougaard, Loli Bahia, Ned Sims, and Sen Samysheva. Captured by David Sims, the campaign shapes a portrait of Balenciaga today.

“I chose individuals, not characters. Human beings with distinct stories, faces marked by experience, vulnerability, and nuance. I was not looking for constructed personas, but for real presence. At the center of Summer 26 is the creation of a new community—different, yet connected by shared values: respect, sensitivity, strength, freedom. Not sameness, but resonance.” - Pierpaolo Piccioli
 
Discover Summer 26, now available in stores and on https://www.balenciaga.com/

Actress Naomi Watts attended the 2024 Met Gala in a custom Balenciaga Tablecloth Couture Dress, which was upcycled from a black lace garment embroidered with jet beads and sequins.

description:
For the 2024 Met Gala, brand ambassador actress Nicole Kidman wore a custom Balenciaga gown
that directly referenced a Couture piece designed and created by Cristóbal Balenciaga in 1951. The original piece was immortalized by Richard Avedon on Dorian Leigh in April of that year, for Harper’s Bazaar. 

This dress is made of a white double silk satin bustier with a tail, and is worn over a long, flared skirt with hand-frayed organza and feather-like embroidery.  

The dress was replicated from an original Cristobal Balenciaga sketch. The final garment differs slightly from the original idea, in that the front of the skirt is a perfect ellipse and not an indented curve.  

This unique piece took about 400 hours to create. It involved intricate hand-detailing in collaboration with Amal Embroideries on approximately 3,000 petals made from 150 meters of fabric. The embroidery was studied to replicate the vivid movement captured in the Avedon photograph. 

Inspired by his Spanish heritage, Cristóbal Balenciaga reinterpreted a flamenco dancer’s full, flounced dress. In his version, black organza petals cascade down the front of the skirt, softly framed by the cutaway of a removable white cotton overdress. This stunning modernization of an iconic design embodies the timelessness of the House’s Couture heritage, founded by M. Balenciaga and evolved today by Demna.

description:
Representing 1930s fashion, Isabelle wore a gown based on a wedding dress designed by her ancestors, the Callot Soeurs, while attending the 2024 Met Gala.

From the end of the 19th century until the 1930s, the Callot Soeurs was a prominent lace couture house. The group dressed empress Sissi, was quoted in Marcel Proust literature, and was greatly admired by Paul Poiret.

Strongly evocative of 1930s fashion with its sleek look and subtle sophistication, this wedding gown is composed of a turtleneck top worn over a dramatic dress. A four-meter train finishes the look.

Particular attention is paid to the details, as each piece is finished with handmade flat hems. A delicate patina is added to the bottom of the skirt, which is an authentic homage to the archival design. The gown pays tribute to the traditions of couture, the Callot Soeurs design, and Ms. Huppert’s legacy. 

This creation was brought to life by the skilled artisans of Atelier Anne Gelgard, a renowned Parisian workshop celebrated for its mastery of fabric manipulation and treatment. With 20 meters of material and 300 hours of work, modifications were made from the original design, including changes to the collar, a construction split into two parts, and the addition of shoulder pads.

Unlike the original ensemble, which comprised a blouse and skirt, our rendition seamlessly blends blouse and dress elements. The neckline was refined for a more tailored fit, and internally bound seams of organza add a flawless finis

Brand ambassador Michelle Yeoh wore a Balenciaga Couture custom gown during the Met Gala on Monday night.

Taking inspiration from Cristóbal Balenciaga Ballroom gowns from the 1940’s, this dress is made of aluminum material, allowing the Balenciaga teams to sculpt the material, fixing the movement in intricate draping. 

The bustier top, slightly disconnected from the body, stands on its own and enhances the upper part of the body. Three fittings were essential to achieve the perfect fit, refining every curve and contour. In total, 200 hours of dedicated work were invested in bringing this gown to life, resulting in a masterpiece of timeless beauty and grace. Two pockets on the side allow an effortless attitude and add a note of modernity to this Couture gown.

The innovative sculptural concept of this extraordinary piece was conceptualized by Demna, a continuation of a technique previously used in his Couture collections that embodies contemporary creativity and abstracts the passage of time.
